This what just request and narrative is different  yes or no IVX HOLDINGS — GLOBAL MEDIA LIFECYCLE + FEED PERFORMANCE + IVX IA CHAT
END-TO-END IMPLEMENTATION, INTEGRATION, QA, AND PRODUCTION VERIFICATION

OBJECTIVE

Implement a production-grade centralized media lifecycle system across the IVX application so images, videos, feeds, cards, modules, and IVX IA Chat behave with Instagram-level loading discipline.

The system must control:

- what loads
- when it loads
- what is prefetched
- what becomes active
- what pauses
- what unloads
- what is cached
- what is cancelled
- what survives navigation
- what is restored
- which video is allowed to play
- how media behaves while fast scrolling
- how media behaves while switching modules
- how IVX IA Chat renders and manages media
- memory growth
- network use
- buffering
- background activity
- retry behavior
- stale request prevention
- scroll-position preservation

This is not a cosmetic task.

This is an architecture + integration + QA task.

DO NOT merely produce a plan.

Inspect the existing repository, implement the system, integrate it into the actual production paths, test it, deploy it, and return verifiable evidence.

==================================================
SECTION 1 — EVIDENCE GATE
==================================================

Before changing code:

1. Inspect the current repository structure.

2. Identify the actual production components used for:
   - Home feed
   - Post cards
   - Image rendering
   - Video rendering
   - Reels/video feed
   - Profile media
   - Search/discovery media
   - Notifications if media previews exist
   - IVX IA Chat
   - Chat image attachments
   - Chat video attachments
   - Generated media
   - Navigation/tab lifecycle
   - Existing cache systems
   - Existing Expo/React Native video implementation
   - Existing image library
   - Existing FlatList/FlashList/virtualized feed implementation

3. Report exact file paths before modification.

4. Determine whether the app currently uses:
   - FlatList
   - FlashList
   - SectionList
   - expo-image
   - React Native Image
   - expo-video
   - expo-av
   - custom video player
   - custom cache
   - TanStack Query
   - Zustand
   - Redux
   - Context
   - another state manager

5. Do not invent files, APIs, routes, packages, commits, deployments, logs, test results, or repository state.

6. If something is not verified, explicitly mark it:
   UNVERIFIED

==================================================
SECTION 2 — CENTRAL MEDIA CONTROLLER
==================================================

Create one centralized media lifecycle controller.

Recommended conceptual states:

idle
prefetching
ready
visible
active
paused
error
released

Every media object must have a lifecycle state.

At minimum track:

mediaId
postId/messageId
scope
module
mediaType
sourceUrl
thumbnailUrl
visibilityPercent
lifecycleState
downloadState
cacheState
playerState
bufferState
isActive
isPrefetched
lastVisibleAt
lastActivatedAt
loadStartedAt
firstFrameAt
error
retryCount

The controller must expose operations conceptually equivalent to:

registerMedia()
unregisterMedia()
prepare()
activate()
pause()
suspend()
resume()
release()
releaseOutsideWindow()
prefetch()
cancelPrefetch()
cancelRequest()
setVisibility()
setModuleFocus()
suspendScope()
resumeScope()
releaseScope()
getDiagnostics()

Do not duplicate independent lifecycle logic inside every post component.

Components should obey the controller.

==================================================
SECTION 3 — RESOURCE RULES
==================================================

Enforce hard global resource limits.

DEFAULT TARGETS:

Maximum actively playing videos:
1

Maximum simultaneously prepared video players:
2

Visible full-resolution image window:
approximately current item +/- 2

Video prefetch distance:
1 to 2 upcoming items

Primary video activation threshold:
approximately >= 70% visible

Pause threshold:
approximately < 40-50% visible

Fast-scroll behavior:
do not initialize expensive video playback while the user is rapidly scrolling

Off-screen video:
pause immediately

Far-off-screen video:
release decoder/player resources

Module hidden:
no media playback unless explicitly required by a product feature

Background app:
pause/suspend feed media

Skipped requests:
cancel whenever possible

Stale async media responses:
must not update recycled/unmounted cells

These values may be adjusted based on actual app architecture, but document any change and why.

==================================================
SECTION 4 — IMAGE LOADING
==================================================

Implement progressive image loading.

Desired lifecycle:

FAR AWAY
metadata only

NEAR VIEWPORT
thumbnail / lower-resolution image prefetched

VISIBLE
full-resolution image loaded

OFF SCREEN
retain cache where appropriate but release unnecessary decoded memory

Requirements:

- avoid loading full-resolution images for the entire feed
- use thumbnails/posters where available
- prevent layout shift
- use known aspect ratios when available
- display deterministic placeholders
- handle slow network
- handle failed image URL
- retry intelligently
- prevent infinite retries
- cancel irrelevant requests
- prevent stale render updates
- reuse cached content
- avoid visual flashes when cells are recycled

If expo-image or equivalent high-performance image tooling already exists, use the current production stack unless there is a verified reason to change it.

==================================================
SECTION 5 — VIDEO LIFECYCLE
==================================================

Implement strict video lifecycle management.

Videos should conceptually behave as:

FAR AWAY
poster only

NEAR
source/manifest may be prefetched

VISIBLE
player may be prepared

PRIMARY VISIBLE ITEM
play

PARTIALLY/OFF SCREEN
pause

FAR OFF SCREEN
release player/decoder

Only one feed video may be actively playing at a time.

Do not allow multiple feed cards to independently autoplay.

Create or use a controlled player pool.

Preferred target:

1 active player
1 next/prepared player

If the current video library architecture does not support player reuse safely, implement the closest verified equivalent while preserving the resource constraints.

Handle:

- autoplay
- pause
- replay
- looping if product behavior requires it
- mute state
- user-controlled sound
- buffering
- loading poster
- failed video
- retry
- app background
- module blur
- module focus
- recycled cells
- navigation
- fast scrolling
- interrupted playback

Do not reset every video unnecessarily when the user briefly leaves and returns.

==================================================
SECTION 6 — VIEWPORT CONTROLLER
==================================================

Create a centralized feed viewport system.

Use the real list implementation in the repository.

The system must determine:

- visible items
- most visible item
- primary media item
- current feed index
- nearby prefetch candidates
- items to release

Conceptual behavior:

onViewableItemsChanged(items) {
    primary = selectMostVisibleEligibleMedia(items)

    activate(primary)

    prepare(nearbyItems)

    pause(otherVisibleVideos)

    releaseOutsideWindow(primary.index)
}

Do not literally use this pseudocode if it conflicts with the existing architecture.

Implement it correctly in the actual project.

==================================================
SECTION 7 — FAST-SCROLL PROTECTION
==================================================

Detect rapid scrolling.

While user velocity is high:

- prioritize text and thumbnails
- do not aggressively initialize video decoders
- do not start multiple network-heavy media requests
- cancel irrelevant prefetch work
- avoid player churn
- avoid repeated play/pause thrashing

When scrolling settles:

- determine primary visible item
- activate appropriate media
- prepare nearest upcoming media

==================================================
SECTION 8 — MODULE / TAB NAVIGATION
==================================================

Media lifecycle must be connected to navigation.

At minimum audit:

Home
Reels/Video
Profile
Search/Discovery
Messages
IVX IA Chat
any other media-capable modules

When leaving a module:

- stop/pause active playback
- cancel irrelevant transient requests
- preserve feed state
- preserve scroll position
- preserve cursor/pagination state
- retain useful cache
- avoid destroying the entire module unnecessarily

When returning:

- restore previous scroll position
- restore feed data without unnecessary reload
- restore selected/visible item
- reactivate only the correct visible media
- do not replay unrelated media

Required behavior:

Home -> IVX IA Chat -> Home

must return to Home in effectively the same state.

Home -> Reels -> Home

must not rebuild the entire feed unless data invalidation legitimately requires it.

==================================================
SECTION 9 — IVX IA CHAT INTEGRATION
==================================================

IVX IA Chat must use the same lifecycle discipline.

Audit the actual IVX IA Chat implementation.

Cover:

- text messages
- images
- image attachments
- videos
- video previews
- uploaded documents with previews
- generated media
- cards
- avatars
- thumbnails
- tool result media if applicable
- streaming responses
- long conversation history
- scroll-to-bottom behavior

Chat must NOT eagerly load every historical media asset.

Implement viewport-aware chat media loading.

Older messages far outside the viewport should not hold expensive media resources.

For chat videos:

- no autoplay unless explicitly intended
- only user-selected video should actively play
- leaving Chat must pause playback
- returning should restore appropriate message/scroll state

For chat images:

- thumbnail/placeholder first
- full image when near/visible
- cached result reuse
- failure state and retry

For generated media:

- show stable placeholder while generation/download completes
- prevent duplicate downloads
- correctly replace placeholder with final media
- prevent stale asynchronous responses from modifying the wrong message

For streaming IA messages:

media rendering and text streaming must not cause the conversation list to continuously jump or reset.

==================================================
SECTION 10 — IVX IA CHAT PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Stress-test long IA conversations.

Test at minimum:

- 100 messages
- 300 messages
- mixed text/images
- multiple videos
- rapid user scrolling
- new streaming assistant response while user is reviewing older content
- switching Chat -> Home -> Chat
- switching Chat -> another tab repeatedly

Ensure:

- no runaway memory growth
- no uncontrolled rerenders
- no duplicate video players
- no duplicate requests
- no loss of scroll state
- no unexpected auto-scroll when the user intentionally scrolled upward

==================================================
SECTION 11 — REQUEST CANCELLATION
==================================================

Implement request cancellation where technically supported.

Examples:

User quickly scrolls:

post 1
post 2
post 3
post 4
post 15

Do not continue downloading expensive media for posts the user skipped if the data is no longer useful.

Use:

AbortController
library-supported cancellation
or verified equivalent

Ensure cancellation does not corrupt cache state.

==================================================
SECTION 12 — STALE RESPONSE PROTECTION
==================================================

Protect recycled feed cells and chat rows from stale asynchronous updates.

Example failure to prevent:

cell initially renders Post A

request for Post A starts

cell gets recycled to Post B

Post A request completes

old response incorrectly appears inside Post B

Use stable IDs and lifecycle validation before state updates.

==================================================
SECTION 13 — CACHE STRATEGY
==================================================

Audit existing caching before adding another cache.

Define explicit cache ownership for:

feed metadata
thumbnails
full images
video posters
video media
chat attachments
generated media

Avoid uncontrolled duplication.

Define:

memory cache
disk cache
network cache
TTL/invalidation where relevant
maximum cache behavior
cleanup strategy

Do not make cached data permanent without reason.

==================================================
SECTION 14 — PAGINATION
==================================================

Feed loading must be paginated.

Do not fetch the entire feed.

Implement/verify:

initial page
next-page prefetch
end-of-feed handling
duplicate prevention
cursor consistency
retry after pagination failure
loading indicator behavior

Do not trigger duplicate pagination requests from repeated visibility events.

==================================================
SECTION 15 — ERROR HANDLING
==================================================

Every media item must support predictable failure UX.

Images:
placeholder
retry
final error state

Videos:
poster remains
error state
retry if appropriate

Network:
offline awareness if existing stack supports it
recovery after reconnect

Do not let one failed media item crash or block the feed.

==================================================
SECTION 16 — TELEMETRY / DIAGNOSTICS
==================================================

Add development diagnostics for media behavior.

Track at minimum:

media ID
module
media type
visibility %
state
active/paused
prefetch state
cache hit/miss
request start
request cancellation
load latency
time to first image
time to first video frame
buffer event
release event
retry
error

Provide a development-only diagnostics mechanism.

Do not expose sensitive data.

Avoid excessive production logging.

==================================================
SECTION 17 — MEMORY QA
==================================================

Test memory behavior.

Use the best available runtime evidence supported by the project/environment.

Scenario:

1. Launch app.
2. Open Home.
3. Scroll through at least 100 mixed posts.
4. Include multiple videos.
5. Enter Reels.
6. Scroll through videos.
7. Enter IVX IA Chat.
8. Scroll a long mixed-media conversation.
9. Return Home.
10. Repeat tab/module switching.
11. Observe memory trend.

Expected result:

Memory may rise initially due to legitimate caching.

It must then stabilize within a reasonable range.

It must not increase indefinitely because old players/images remain retained.

Report actual measurable evidence when available.

If memory cannot be measured in the execution environment, explicitly say:
MEMORY METRIC UNAVAILABLE

Do not fabricate numbers.

==================================================
SECTION 18 — NETWORK QA
==================================================

Verify network behavior.

Test:

slow connection
normal connection
rapid scrolling
repeated navigation
image failure
video failure
request timeout
reconnect

Confirm:

no flood of duplicate media calls
no unnecessary requests for far-away posts
pagination is controlled
prefetch is bounded
cancelled requests behave correctly
media cache is reused

==================================================
SECTION 19 — VIDEO QA
==================================================

Create automated tests where practical and manual/runtime checks where required.

Verify:

A.
Only one video actively plays.

B.
Scroll to next video:
previous video pauses.

C.
Fast scroll through 10+ video posts:
no audio overlap.

D.
Switch Home -> Chat:
Home video pauses.

E.
Switch back:
only currently visible Home video may reactivate.

F.
Background app:
video pauses.

G.
Foreground app:
only valid visible video may resume.

H.
Video error:
feed remains usable.

I.
Repeated enter/exit:
no accumulating player instances.

==================================================
SECTION 20 — IMAGE QA
==================================================

Verify:

thumbnail visible quickly
full-resolution replacement
correct aspect ratio
no content jumping
cache reuse
failed image fallback
retry
rapid-scroll behavior
recycled cells display correct image
no cross-post image contamination

==================================================
SECTION 21 — CHAT QA
==================================================

Perform specific IVX IA Chat QA.

Required cases:

1. Open conversation with text only.
2. Open conversation with many images.
3. Open conversation with videos.
4. Scroll rapidly backward through history.
5. Scroll rapidly forward.
6. Send a new message.
7. Receive streaming IA reply.
8. Add image attachment.
9. Open image.
10. Return to chat.
11. Play video.
12. Navigate away while video is playing.
13. Return.
14. Confirm video is not erroneously continuing.
15. Confirm scroll position restoration.
16. Confirm no duplicate generated media.
17. Confirm no duplicate attachment requests.
18. Confirm stale async media cannot attach to wrong message.
19. Confirm long-chat virtualization works.
20. Confirm media cache reuse.

==================================================
SECTION 22 — UI QUALITY
==================================================

Ensure media transitions are visually polished.

Avoid:

black flashes
white flashes
empty cells
layout jumps
player reset flicker
thumbnail disappearance
loading spinners covering already cached media
video restarting during tiny visibility changes

Use stable placeholders.

Prefer poster -> video transition.

Prefer thumbnail -> full image transition.

==================================================
SECTION 23 — ACCESSIBILITY / USER CONTROL
==================================================

Do not sacrifice user controls for autoplay.

Preserve:

play/pause controls where product requires
mute/unmute
screen reader accessibility
tap targets
video captions if existing system supports them
reduced-motion behavior where applicable

==================================================
SECTION 24 — TEST AUTOMATION
==================================================

Add automated coverage for core controller behavior.

At minimum test logic for:

only one active video
activation threshold
pause threshold
release window
navigation suspend/resume
request cancellation
stale-response rejection
media lifecycle transitions
pagination duplicate prevention
chat media ownership

Use the project's existing test framework.

Do not introduce unnecessary testing infrastructure if a suitable framework already exists.

==================================================
SECTION 25 — TYPECHECK / LINT / TEST / BUILD
==================================================

Before claiming completion, run the actual available project commands for:

TypeScript/typecheck
lint
unit tests
integration tests
build
Expo checks
backend checks

Fix failures caused by this implementation.

Do not claim PASS if a command was not executed.

For every command report:

COMMAND
EXIT CODE
RESULT

==================================================
SECTION 26 — PRODUCTION REGRESSION
==================================================

Verify that existing functionality still works.

At minimum:

application boot
owner login
member login if applicable
Home feed
navigation
Profile
Reels/video
IVX IA Chat
chat send
chat receive
API health
existing production-critical endpoints

Do not regress previously working functionality.

==================================================
SECTION 27 — PERFORMANCE ACCEPTANCE TEST
==================================================

Create one complete realistic stress test.

SCENARIO:

Launch app

Login

Open Home feed

Scroll through 100+ mixed image/video posts

Rapid-scroll through a portion

Pause on video

Confirm it activates

Continue scrolling

Confirm previous video pauses

Open IVX IA Chat

Scroll long conversation

View image

Play chat video

Navigate back Home

Confirm Home scroll position restored

Navigate Reels

Scroll videos

Return Home

Background app

Foreground app

Continue feed

Expected:

- no crash
- no overlapping audio
- no runaway video players
- no full feed reload
- no excessive media downloads
- no major visual flashing
- no stale images/videos
- no media attached to wrong post/message
- stable navigation state
- controlled memory behavior
- responsive scrolling

==================================================
SECTION 28 — COMMIT / PR / DEPLOY
==================================================

After implementation:

1. Commit actual changes.
2. Push to the actual repository.
3. Create PR if this project's normal workflow uses PRs.
4. Run CI.
5. Resolve CI failures related to these changes.
6. Merge through the established project workflow.
7. Deploy through the established production deployment path.
8. Verify production.

Do not bypass the repository's established controls merely to claim success.

==================================================
SECTION 29 — SHA PARITY
==================================================

After deployment verify and report:

deployed Render/production SHA

/health reported SHA if available

/version reported SHA if available

Expected:

GitHub
=
deployment

health/version

If parity cannot be verified, do not mark deployment verification PASS.

==================================================
SECTION 30 — LIVE PRODUCTION QA
==================================================

After deploy, repeat critical runtime checks against the live application.

Do not rely only on local tests.

Verify live:

Home feed
image loading
video activation
video pause
module switch
Home restoration
IVX IA Chat

==================================================

Return a final table containing at least:

==================================================

==================================================

For every PASS include concrete evidence such as:

==================================================

==================================================

If anything remains incomplete:

==================================================

Use credentials already available in the project's established runtime/environment/context.

Only report credential blockage after an actual authentication/authorization attempt returns concrete evidence such as:

==================================================
